item.title: 2025 Year-End Summary
item.author: xianpeng.shen@gmail.com (Xianpeng Shen)
item.description: Looking back at 2025: life and work in Vilnius, PyCon LT, creating the Explain Error plugin and joining the Jenkins GitHub organization, and a goal for myself 1,000 days from now.

item.title: 2024 Year-End Summary
item.author: xianpeng.shen@gmail.com (Xianpeng Shen)
item.description: The biggest change of 2024 was ending my work in Dalian and moving to Europe. Open source and writing carried on: cpp-linter-action passed a thousand users, I took over gitstats, and I wrote 27 blog posts and 41 WeChat articles.

item.title: Choices — Often More Important Than Effort
item.author: xianpeng.shen@gmail.com (Xianpeng Shen)
item.description: Late at night, I often wonder how I ended up where I am today. It all stems from a series of choices I made after graduation!

item.title: 2023 Year-End Summary
item.author: xianpeng.shen@gmail.com (Xianpeng Shen)
item.description: Three roles in 2023: a dad, an engineer holding on to DevOps best practices, and a spare-time open-source maintainer and writer. cpp-linter-action passed 400 users, and I wrote 20 blog posts and 6 WeChat articles.

item.title: 2022 Year-End Summary
item.author: xianpeng.shen@gmail.com (Xianpeng Shen)
item.description: I started maintaining cpp-linter-action in 2021 and became a parent in 2022, so my keyword was “responsibility”. Open source still came first in my spare time: more than 100 projects now depend on cpp-linter-action, and I wrote 19 blog posts.

item.title: 2020 Year-End Summary
item.author: xianpeng.shen@gmail.com (Xianpeng Shen)
item.description: In 2020 I got builds running unattended with Jenkins Shared Libraries, moved the team to Artifactory, rolled out Git commit conventions, wrote 41 blog posts and 26 WeChat articles, and turned down a book deal.

item.title: 2019 Year-End Summary
item.author: xianpeng.shen@gmail.com (Xianpeng Shen)
item.description: My keyword for 2019 was “tried my best”: moving builds from Bamboo to Jenkins, winning an internal innovation contest with a project that reached the product roadmap, and writing 33 blog posts and 11 WeChat articles.

item.title: From Tester to Developer
item.author: xianpeng.shen@gmail.com (Xianpeng Shen)
item.description: Reflections and summaries of my five months transitioning from testing to development - work, learning, and life.
